title: A. G. Cook
summary: This document is a Wikipedia-style biographical article about A. G. Cook (Alexander Guy Cook), an English record producer and founder of the influential record label PC Music. The article begins with an overview of Cook's career, highlighting his role in developing and popularizing the hyperpop genre and his work as executive producer for Charli XCX. The "Early life" section covers his family background as the son of architect Sir Peter Cook, his education at King Alfred School and Goldsmiths, University of London, and his first musical project Dux Content with collaborator Danny L Harle. The "Career" section is organized chronologically, detailing his early experiments from 2011–2013, the founding of PC Music in 2013 and early singles like "Keri Baby" and "Hey QT," his extensive production work with Charli XCX on mixtapes and albums (Number 1 Angel, Pop 2, Charli, How I'm Feeling Now, Brat), the release of his solo albums 7G and Apple in 2020, collaborations with artists such as Hikaru Utada, Jónsi, Lady Gaga, and Beyoncé (earning a Grammy nomination for "All Up in Your Mind"), and recent activities including the closure of PC Music, his 2024 album Britpop, and his first Grammy win for Best Dance/Electronic Album for Brat. Additional sections describe his artistry and production techniques, the PC Music label's aesthetic and influence, his personal life including his relationship with musician Alaska Reid, and listings of his discography, filmography, awards, and external links.
